entries.title: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
entries.summary:
The Remote Agents Platform turned engineering tasks into API calls: teams delegate the work, execution takes place in a remote sandbox, and the result comes back as a merge request. In the internal security platform, the number of vulnerabilities fixed more than doubled.

## The challenge isn’t the task—it’s the scale

iFood maintains more than 15,000 code repositories. Each periodically needs specific tasks performed: validating code to ensure it meets internal standards, fixing vulnerable dependencies, or running an analysis.

None of these tasks is difficult on its own. The challenge comes when those tasks multiply.

“Solving this for one repository is easy. The challenge is solving it at scale,” says Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer at iFood. “The Remote Agents Platform is designed to make it possible to solve this at scale across all 15,000 repositories.”

Before the platform, each team tackled the problem in its own way—and they all ran into the same obstacle.

“Before, we had fragmented solutions. Imagine several teams at iFood trying to solve different problems, but without this layer, this agentic runtime, available to them. In the end, those solutions always ran into the same problem.”

What was missing wasn’t intelligence or a use case. It was execution infrastructure. A dedicated _runtime_.

> “Teams can focus on solving their business problems and delegate execution to our platform.”

—Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer, iFood

## A coding agent in the cloud, accessible through an API

The team describes the Remote Agents Platform as an API that launches a remote agentic coding task. The cycle has three steps: the user submits a prompt and environment requirements through a REST call; the platform processes the task on a dedicated remote runner inside an isolated sandbox; and the result is retrieved later.

“The platform’s entry point, its interface, is a simple REST API. Users can use this API to create the runs they need. Internally, we handle and manage the entire lifecycle and delegate execution to isolated sandboxes,” he explains. Task progress can be monitored in real time.

The runner’s internal design alternates between two different types of steps—and that combination makes the overall workflow predictable.

Deterministic steps bookend the workflow: cloning the repository, importing the _skills_ the agent can use, and setting up the working branch at the start; publishing the merge request and making the generated artifacts available at the end. In between is the agentic execution itself, running GPT‑5.6 Luna inside the sandbox.

“It’s a combination of those two things: deterministic steps and agentic execution within the workflow.”

The sandbox runs Ubuntu and includes the toolchains iFood’s ecosystem requires—Python, Java, Kotlin, C#, TypeScript, Rust, JavaScript, and Go—along with general-purpose tools. Beyond the sandbox, the agent can access Nexus, GitLab, Docker, Snyk, Kubernetes, and AWS.

## Why GPT‑5.6 Luna

The model choice came down to three factors considered together, rather than just one.

“We chose GPT‑5.6 Luna because, among models at the same checkpoint, the benchmarks showed it offered a great balance of intelligence, efficiency, and execution speed—how quickly it could complete tasks. Those three qualities together led us to choose GPT‑5.6 Luna.”

That balance matters more for a platform built to scale than it would for a one-off use case. With tens of thousands of tokens being consumed, the average cost of four U.S. cents per run stops being a minor detail and becomes an architectural consideration.

> “Given our plans to scale the platform across many use cases at iFood, the balance of efficiency and intelligence that OpenAI’s model provides ensures we can scale sustainably.”

—Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer, iFood

## How to tell whether the agent completed the task

Delegating execution at scale creates a new challenge: automatically determining whether the agent did what it was supposed to do.

iFood’s answer comes in the step after the session. Once execution is complete, the result is processed using OpenAI’s Structured Outputs, which requires the output to conform to a predefined contract.

> “We process the result using Structured Outputs, which ensures the response follows a predefined contract. From the agent’s session, we can identify the outputs within the response structure we expect. This helps reduce uncertainty and ensures we can always get a response from the agent’s session, whether positive or negative.”

—Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer, iFood

## The first major user: security

The platform already powers an internal iFood security product that scans the 15,000 repositories for vulnerable dependencies and attempts to fix them.

The migration had a direct impact: “With our platform, the accuracy of those changes, those fixes, more than doubled,” says Coelho.

This use case illustrates the idea behind the platform: the security team didn’t need to build its own agentic runtime or become experts in agent orchestration. It needed to call an API.

## Asynchronous execution gives developers their time back

The team emphasizes what asynchronous execution frees developers to do, rather than replacement.

Because the task is delegated and runs without supervision, the developer doesn’t have to stay focused on monitoring it.

“While they’re in a meeting, they can launch a code fix, a performance analysis, or another task that’s a little more routine—something they can delegate without having to monitor it at that moment.”

Routine work no longer competes for the team’s attention. That leaves time for problems that require judgment.

> “You can unlock those productivity gains without necessarily having to monitor the work as it happens.”

—Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer, iFood

## Modeled on the APIs that inspired it

The Remote Agents Platform was designed as an internal layer with similarities to the way OpenAI makes this type of task available to external customers.

“The Remote Agents Platform drew a lot of inspiration from OpenAI’s APIs, both the Batch API and the Agents API, which is an even more recent OpenAI product. We built a platform that resembles those products, but is internal to iFood.”

The inspiration went beyond the concept. It extends to the design of the interfaces, the organization of resources, and the approach to asynchronous execution with results retrieved later.

> “These products directly inspired how we built our solution.”

—Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer, iFood

## Results at a glance

*   The platform has completed more than 25,000 tasks, consuming more than 27 billion tokens, at an average cost of US$0.04 per run.

*   After migrating to the Remote Agents Platform, the internal security platform more than doubled both the accuracy of its fixes and the number of vulnerabilities resolved.

*   Coverage extends across iFood’s more than 15,000 code repositories.

*   All runs use GPT‑5.6 Luna, chosen for its balance of intelligence, efficiency, and speed.

*   Structured Outputs ensures that each session returns a result that follows a predefined contract, whether positive or negative.

*   Product teams have moved from building fragmented solutions to delegating agentic execution through a REST API.

## Lessons for leaders

*   **The bottleneck is often the runtime, not the use case.** Several teams already knew what they wanted to automate; they lacked an environment in which to run it.

*   **Combine deterministic steps with agentic execution.** Cloning, publishing, and making artifacts available don’t require a model; the complex task in between does.

*   **Treat cost per run as an architectural decision.** At scale, the cost per task determines what is feasible to automate.

*   **Require outputs to follow a contract.** Without a structured response, there’s no way to know at scale whether the agent achieved its objective.

*   **Asynchronous execution is the real productivity gain.** The value lies in not having to monitor the work, rather than completing it faster while watching over it.

## Tips

*   Expose agentic capabilities through an internal API so other teams can use them without rebuilding the infrastructure.

*   Isolate each run in its own sandbox, with your ecosystem’s toolchains already installed.

*   Choose a model by considering intelligence, cost, and speed together, rather than a single benchmark.

*   Use structured outputs to classify success and failure automatically.

*   Start with an internal user with a clear pain point and high volume—at iFood, that was the security platform.

## Next steps

The team plans to bring the platform to many more use cases across iFood, expanding the range of internal products that delegate agentic execution to it—with cost per task determining whether that expansion can be sustained.

entries.summary:
- [Other] Added skills from MCP servers (beta). They show as server:skill in the / menu; other skills keep their names
- [Other] Added a PreSkillShellCommand hook event that can refuse a skill or command's inline shell commands as it loads; on 2.1.331 and older, a settings file naming it opens a dialog at start
- [Other] Added "Always deliver" to the prompt for held messages from other sessions
- [Other] Added a footer line that stays while a flagged message has your session on a different model, until you pick one with /model
- [Other] Added an OpenTelemetry assistant_response event for text Claude sends through SendUserMessage or Cowork's message tool, when response logging is on
- [Other] Added a warning in VS Code and Desktop's Code tab when part of a session couldn't be saved, saying how to save it with /compact
- [Other] Added a notice in VS Code and Desktop's Code tab when a resumed session's earlier messages weren't loaded, as the terminal already shows
- [Other] Added your Cyber Verification Program access tier to the startup header, beside the model name when your tier applies to that model and you're signed in with a claude.ai account
- [Other] Fixed claude auth login reporting Login successful. when a claude.ai login could not be saved: it now exits 1 and says what to check, such as a leftover lock file or a full disk
- [Other] Fixed Read, @-mentions and compaction hanging on a named pipe that nothing writes to, such as a .env mounted by a locked secrets manager; the read now fails after 20 seconds
- [Other] Fixed turns ending in "Prompt is too long" after repeated auto-compaction failures when one more compaction at the context limit could have kept them going
- [Other] Fixed compaction failing when a summary kept running past the output limit: after three cut-off replies, the last try now asks for a shorter summary
- [Other] Fixed a freeze when a permission rule or hook condition with several wildcards was checked against a long command
- [Other] Fixed freezes and runaway memory use in most cases while a hook prints output without end
- [Other] Fixed a freeze and context overflow when a hook blocks or fails during a turn, or after /compact, with a very large log; text over about 50,000 characters is now shortened
- [Other] Fixed the terminal freezing, and ignoring Ctrl+C, while a local MCP server floods its standard output
- [Other] Fixed a freeze when a prompt or piped input holds an @ followed by a very long unbroken string, such as minified CSS with an embedded font
- [Other] Fixed a long freeze when opening a rewind point after a large tracked file was rewritten
- [Other] Fixed SSE MCP servers hanging or refusing every tool call after their event stream was cut and came back on a new endpoint or not at all, until reconnected by hand
- [Other] Fixed Remote Control showing a session in the desktop app, VS Code or the Agent SDK as running while it waited there on a dialog or an MCP server's question
- [Other] Fixed a usage limit being reported as reached to Remote Control, IDE and SDK clients after it had already reset
- [Other] Fixed CLAUDE.md and rules files being sent to the model a second time, in most cases, after a session moves into a worktree under .claude/worktrees with EnterWorktree or is resumed there
- [Other] Fixed tool calls that never ran being counted as done in a claude.ai chat's summary line after you declined a permission prompt in a session that had restarted
- [Other] Linux: Fixed the Bash edit diff showing an unchanged symlink as edited after Claude had read the file through it
- [Other] Fixed resuming a session and /stats freezing for seconds when a transcript holds many damaged lines
- [Other] Fixed a family name such as sonnet in --fallback-model being dropped when availableModels allows only an older version of it
- [Other] Fixed keys lagging for seconds while /stats reads large session transcripts, also after the dialog is closed, and with debug logging on while a language server floods its stderr
- [Other] Fixed a session failing when the cloud refused its default model and an availableModels list that isn't enforced named neither it nor an older model of that family
- [Other] Fixed an enforced list of older models failing on Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Foundry when the first is refused: it now steps down to the next in that family, if listed newest first
- [Other] Fixed opus failing on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Foundry behind a gateway that refuses a model in its own words: it now steps down to an older model that answers
- [Other] Fixed the start-up model upgrade offer on Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform naming a model that your availableModels list leaves out
- [Other] Fixed Bedrock sub-agents failing when your account lists no profile for their model in the parent's region: they now use the model's own profile, which can be outside that region
- [Other] Fixed Foundry sessions leaving a model family when an admin's list blocks the version sonnet, opus or haiku points to: they now use its newest allowed version under a built-in or mapped name
- [Other] Fixed the sonnet alias on Bedrock Mantle resolving to Haiku 4.5: it now means Sonnet 5, not Sonnet 5.5, and an account without Sonnet 5 gets an error, so enable it first
- [Other] Fixed Ctrl+C at the prompt starting a new turn, and a double Ctrl+C not exiting, when a background agent it stopped had an unread subagent report
- [Other] Fixed /install-github-app ticking a workflow again after going back with Esc
- [Other] Fixed dictated text past 10,000 characters being lost
- [Other] Fixed raw "JSON Parse error" and "The operation was aborted." API errors when the non-streaming retry got a broken response or was interrupted
- [Other] Fixed Esc not stopping computer use between actions on macOS when Claude Code's window or an app you allowed is in front; an Esc meant for that app's popup now stops computer use instead
- [Other] Fixed a rare hang when a helper command, such as an API key helper, ran past its time limit
- [Other] Fixed selecting text in fullscreen pushing the footer's right-hand label onto a second row, which moved the text under the mouse and could copy the wrong line
- [Other] Fixed a PreToolUse hook's reason for asking not showing on terminal Read, Grep, Glob, Edit and Write prompts (#102892, #105343)
- [Other] Fixed temp_* folders piling up in ~/.claude/plugins/cache when a downloaded plugin couldn't be copied into place
- [Other] Fixed --effort being ignored when starting an interactive session with --environment while CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL is set to the same level
- [Other] Fixed headless and cloud sessions reporting a foreground fork's Agent call as finished the moment the fork started
- [Other] Fixed local MCP servers seeing a new session ID after a Remote Control session's process restarts
- [Other] Fixed idle compaction being skipped for subscribers still well under their weekly limit
- [Other] Fixed an @-mentioned text file with an extension being silently dropped when even its first 2,000 lines exceed the read limit; Claude is now told its size and how to read it
- [Other] Fixed the plugin "not cached" error pointing to /plugin instead of /reload-plugins, the command that reloads plugins
- [Other] Fixed self-hosted runner sessions failing their first clone under Anthropic-managed git when the machine's git config has an includeIf "gitdir:" or (git 2.44 to 2.46) "onbranch:" section
- [Other] Fixed replies that start with phrases like "You've used" or "You've hit your" showing as a red usage limit error
- [Other] Fixed a resumed conversation sometimes missing its last messages after a crash or kill on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Foundry and other third-party providers
- [Other] Fixed NotebookEdit saving an invalid notebook when an edit changes a cell's type; turning a cell with attachments into code is now refused
- [Other] Fixed a long README in a design system moved from standalone Claude Design losing its list of files to load when Claude starts a deck or design
- [Other] Fixed MCP tool calls failing with "malformed task handle" when the server's task ID is longer than 128 characters; IDs of up to 1,024 characters now work
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed --configure-git sometimes reporting a hung git --version as a git that isn't on PATH
- [Other] Fixed task ids being reused and deleted tasks coming back when several tasks were deleted or updated at once, and TaskGet listing completed tasks as blockers
- [Other] Fixed stale and repeated rows in the fullscreen Ctrl+R history picker when prompts share a timestamp
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode silently skipping a tool call whose input has a list of over 4,096 items, and freezing on a very large typed array in a tool's input, which is now refused
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode leaving a message unanswered when it was typed during a command and Esc was pressed before Claude replied; the message now starts a new turn, which a second Esc stops
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode not telling Claude when a slow command moved to the background and left its script with empty output, or of the time limit on background commands in claude -p and the Agent SDK
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode sometimes waiting for minutes on a command that had already been stopped
- [Other] Fixed a typed slash command's inline shell commands not running in Code Mode after a background script's output arrived
- [Other] Fixed Code Mode sessions in the Agent SDK and claude -p sometimes losing Claude's last reply on resume after being stopped while a script was running
- [Other] Remote Control: Fixed sessions hosted by the desktop app or VS Code showing as idle while /compact runs
- [Other] Fixed a session sometimes losing its "needs input" status after a background task's report in Claude Desktop
- [Other] Fixed Grep: -o missing an empty match at the end of a file with no last newline, -o with multiline adding an empty line or misnumbering lines in non-UTF-8 files, and -A and -B ignored beside a zero -C
- [Other] Fixed unbinding a chord in keybindings.json still leaving its first key waiting for a second when it was spelled meta and bound as alt, or the reverse
- [Other] Fixed moving an empty session to the background sometimes failing with "Couldn't load transcript from file"
- [Other] Fixed OpenTelemetry reporting a failed mcp_server_connection event at each start for a built-in server that isn't turned on for the account
- [Other] Fixed Esc not stopping a Bash command while it waited for its file diff in large or slow git repositories, which held the next message
- [Other] Fixed pasted links and relative paths ending in an image file name appearing late and swallowing an Enter pressed right after
- [Other] Fixed /mcp reconnect all and /mcp disable all counting a built-in server that isn't turned on for the account
- [Other] Fixed interrupting a turn while a mod's turn.step hook was waiting showing "user-cancel" as an error instead of "Interrupted"
- [Other] Fixed ~/.claude.json being reported as corrupted when another session was in the middle of saving it
- [Other] Fixed web searches failing with an API error when Claude's list of allowed or blocked domains was empty or had duplicates
- [Other] Fixed resuming a paused workflow in Code Mode waiting for minutes while other background work was running
- [Other] Fixed subagents in Code Mode failing with "Agent stalled" and losing their command when a script ran for more than 10 minutes
- [Other] Improved claude plugin marketplace add on Windows to wait and try again in some cases when another program, such as a virus scanner, briefly holds the downloaded files
- [Other] Windows: Improved stability on some company PCs, where Claude Code could exit with no output shortly after start
- [Other] Improved computer use setup: the Screen Recording permission prompt can now restart Claude Code and resume the chat
- [Other] Improved computer use to take less context until Claude uses it
- [Other] Improved the error when a proxy or gateway cuts or damages a compressed response: a turn now ends in plain words instead of raw "ZlibError fetching" text
- [Other] Improved /context: shorter output in fullscreen, so the total is less likely to scroll off in a short window, and the legend names its unit once
- [Other] Improved peak memory use and speed of /usage on machines with many recent sessions
- [Other] Improved /permissions to refuse a rule that would be skipped at the next start, such as rm -rf with no tool name, and to show the reason
- [Other] Improved resuming a session in Code Mode: Claude is now told up front that its earlier script variables are gone
- [Other] Improved Claude in Code Mode to confirm before discarding worktree changes, to read artifact files before publishing them, and to update an existing artifact instead of creating a second one
- [Other] Improved Code Mode's tool search to show long MCP tool descriptions whole where they fit, as a cut description could lead to wrong calls
- [Other] Linux: Improved the Ctrl+V message to name the package to install (wl-clipboard or xclip) when images can't be read from the clipboard
- [Other] Improved recovery for long conversations behind a proxy or gateway with a request size limit, where every message and /compact failed with a 413
- [Other] Improved Glob speed in large local folders on Windows machines with 6 or more CPUs: folders are walked in parallel, and a search stopped at its time limit now lists what it found
- [Other] Improved memory use when resuming a long conversation
- [Other] Improved memory use at startup with MCP servers that list many tools
- [Other] Improved memory use of claude -p and SDK-hosted sessions at the start of a conversation
- [Other] Updated computer use on macOS to newer safety rules, so some actions are refused and typing can be slower
- [Other] Changed terminal and VS Code sessions moved to Sonnet 5 or 5.5 on Bedrock Mantle, Agent Platform and Foundry to start in auto mode if no mode is set; set disableAutoMode to "disable" to stop it
- [Other] Changed the sonnet model alias on Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry to Sonnet 5.5, and Foundry's opus alias to Opus 5.5; sonnet on Amazon Bedrock stays at Sonnet 4.5
- [Other] Changed the default model on Microsoft Foundry to Sonnet 5.5: deploy claude-sonnet-5-5, or set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL to a model you have deployed
- [Other] Changed sonnet and background requests on Google Cloud's Agent Platform to read VERTEX_REGION_CLAUDE_5_5_SONNET; with only the 4_5 variable set they go to CLOUD_ML_REGION or us-east5
- [Other] Changed --model default and a Default pick to move to an older model when that model isn't available, instead of stopping with an error; in auto mode, only to a model auto mode accepts
- [Other] Changed Microsoft Foundry: Claude Sonnet 4, Opus 4 and Opus 4.1 now count as retired, so step-downs stop above them and a pin to one warns that it was retired
- [Other] Changed the Claude apps gateway's built-in model list: Sonnet 5.5 replaces Sonnet 4.5 as its second model, and Claude Desktop starts on it where a policy allows no Opus 4.6
- [Other] Changed SDK and claude -p mid-turn messages to count as the user's where feature flags aren't fetched, as on clouds or with telemetry off, from Opus 4.8 on; mark relayed text isSynthetic: true
- [Other] Changed computer-use to a reserved skill name on Macs with computer use on: your own skill or command of that name stops loading, and a start-up notice says to rename it
- [Other] Changed the default OpenTelemetry service.name of desktop Code tab sessions to claude-code-desktop; update filters keyed on claude-code, or set OTEL_SERVICE_NAME to keep the old name
- [Other] Changed OpenTelemetry tool_input to show only the length of text sent through SendUserMessage or Cowork's message tool, unless response logging is on (OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=1)
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Changed CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: its prefix can now end in oat02- as well as oat01-. Update proxy rules and log scrubbers that match oat01-, and mask the whole value
- [Other] Changed claude self-hosted-runner setup with no arguments on macOS and Linux to ask for the environment key in the terminal before Claude starts, and to hide it as you paste
- [Other] Changed Claude Desktop's Code tab on Anthropic's API to ignore default, side-request, alias and subagent model ids not starting with claude in your own settings beside a gateway address
- [Other] Changed Claude Desktop's Code tab on Anthropic's API to ignore a CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW under 200K in your own settings beside a gateway address; use /autocompact instead
- [Other] Changed plan mode in the desktop app's Code tab and VS Code to ask for approval instead of refusing when no auto mode safety check can judge a command, for plans entered from Manual or Accept edits
- [Other] Changed PgUp and Home to go to No on destructive questions, such as /clear from an agent's view
- [Other] Changed /feedback drafts in the terminal to open on Not now, above separate rows to send the report alone or with the transcript
- [Other] Changed tap-mode voice dictation to keep the microphone on until 60 seconds without new words or 10 minutes, up from 15 seconds and 2 minutes, then keep the text unsent; the next tap adds to it
- [Other] Changed tap-mode voice dictation to stop when you send the prompt, and to stop and say why when you edit it, a panel covers it, or the connection or a separate recorder program is lost
- [Other] Changed /schedule, permission prompts and /loop's cloud offer to say "cloud scheduled task" instead of "routine" or "cloud schedule"; /routines still works
- [Other] Changed model switches from the Claude mobile app or claude.ai to keep the effort level you saved for the previous model when none is saved for the new one
- [Other] Changed the hint a mod's PromptHint hook receives to leave out the hint for selected text when the fullscreen footer has a label on its right
- [Other] Changed awsCredentialExport to time out after 10 minutes instead of waiting forever
- [Other] [VSCode] Added a notification in more cases when closing a proposed diff leaves the edit unapplied, and stopped the diff notifications on a split copy of an answered diff
- [Other] [VSCode] Added a warning when restoring a conversation with /rewind in the side bar stops a self-paced /loop
- [Other] [VSCode] Added the installed version to the rows of Manage plugins
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed Rewind staying on "Checking code changes…" while Claude's process hung at its start
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the model picker's arrow keys starting from the wrong row right after it opens, and screen readers not announcing its highlighted model when opened with /model or the command menu
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the diff view's "Copy deleted line" and "Copy changed line" copying a different line than they name, and a double-click near the bottom copying unasked
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the blocked microphone's tooltip being cut off, long addresses running out of Web Fetch rows, usage bars looking full in High Contrast, and a Thinking row jumping away when clicked
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed a second Logout in the same window reporting success while the first was still running, and added a Show logs button to the error when logout fails
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the chat showing no notice when a background command, agent, workflow or monitor finished while Claude was idle
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed forking a conversation, opening and saving memories, and creating project output styles failing on NTFS drives in VS Code 1.101 and 1.102 on Windows 11 24H2 and later
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed Web Fetch showing "Fetched from" with a success dot when the site returned an error or a redirect that wasn't followed
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the compaction summary showing as your own prompt, and in Rewind and prompt history, after reloading, resuming or forking a compacted conversation
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed spinnerVerbs from Claude Code user and managed settings being ignored
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed right-to-left text from mods showing its punctuation on the wrong side, and a mod's band or pane filling only part of its width when the panel font has no box-drawing characters
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed an empty, locked editor pane staying beside the next file or Claude tab after the last Claude tab was closed
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed a session rename that cannot be saved reverting silently, and screen readers not hearing a session's status, which session is open or which groups are collapsed
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed a hidden panel's notice not naming the waiting session, Hebrew and Arabic questions reading out of order, and a question cut off when Claude's process ended showing only a red dot
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed a sign-in that failed with no error message returning to the sign-in screen with nothing shown, and an authentication error still looking current after you signed in again in that tab
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the chat moving when a menu opened over some banners, and an agent's tool call count shrinking in long sessions; it now shows how many of the calls are listed
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed most links to files without an extension, to folders, and with a line and column doing nothing
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed queued messages and attached files showing in reverse order after a conversation was reopened
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed a question that ended in an error showing "Something went wrong" when its stored result had no text
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed redacted thinking showing as "Unsupported content type"
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the message box not underlining the word that an input method (IME) is composing
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed a held Up key replacing an unsent message with an earlier prompt, and Down not bringing the message back after the recalled prompt got a new line or was cleared
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed /model completed with Tab sometimes switching the model, and closing the model picker right away when nothing is running
- [Other] [VSCode] Improved the time it takes to open the Claude panel and long sessions, performance while long replies stream, and the speed of reading diagnostics in very large workspaces
- [Other] [VSCode] Improved commands and one-line output opened in a plain text tab: they now wrap
- [Other] [VSCode] Changed voice dictation to stop by itself after 60 seconds without recognized speech or 10 minutes, up from 15 seconds and 2 minutes, so the microphone can stay on longer

entries.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
entries.summary:
24th November 2026

I gave a keynote at the [AI Engineer Code Summit](https://ai.engineer/code/2026) a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months.

Here’s [the video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9RKrSF9d2SE) of the talk. In this post I’m going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply.

#### Coding agents in November 2025

Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of [Claude Opus 4.5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-5). With hindsight, this was a consequential model.

In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said:

> Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. They said that tasks that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 just a few weeks ago are now within reach.

This held up.

Claude Code was 9 months old at that point, having been [introduced alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-7-sonnet) on February 24th, 2025.

Opus 4.5 was the first model I had used with Claude Code where the default result was generally the right thing. I hadn’t been using Claude Code as a daily driver because it didn’t feel reliable enough—I had to correct it often enough that it didn’t feel like a clear accelerant.

The new Opus changed that. For most of the coding problems I faced on a daily basis, Opus would _get them right_. It was clearly faster than working through the problems myself.

Also in November, OpenAI released GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex, and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. These had a similar effect on their Codex coding agent: it became reliably useful for many of my coding tasks.

The timing was convenient, because the December holidays were upon us. A lot of people, myself included, spent December tinkering with these new tools to see what they could do. By January we were ready to use them for our actual work.

#### Fable class models in June/July

We got our first hint of Claude Fable in April, when Anthropic announced Claude Mythos and [said that it was _too dangerous_ to release](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Apr/7/project-glasswing/), due to its improved cybersecurity capabilities. Mythos was a model that could not just find security vulnerabilities, it could also figure out how to exploit them.

In June we got to see how good that model was for ourselves, with the release of Claude Fable 5—a defanged Mythos, that would solve most problems but would actively block you from using it for security work.

After three glorious days... the US government took it away from us. Fable 5 was placed under export controls that effectively banned the model. We wouldn’t get it back until July 1st.

For me, Fable was an inflection point because it introduced us to what I now think of as **Fable class models**. My definition of these:

In June I wrote about how [Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jun/11/fable-is-relentlessly-proactive/), after I asked it to help fix a display glitch in Safari and it spun up its own `pyobjc-framework-Quartz` screenshot mechanism and a CORS-enabled localhost logging server to help resolve the bug.

A more recent example of the power of Fable class models is my [mysterious beep finder](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/9/mysterious-beeps/) from a couple of weeks ago. I gave Opus 5.5 and then Fable 5.2 access to five WebAudio microphones in a room full of boxes and it was able to triangulate the source of an infuriating mysterious beep to within about 40cm.

Give it a goal, give it the right tools, and watch it cook.

I’d currently class Claude Fable 5, 5.1, 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 as Fable class (I think of Opus 5.5 as “cheap Fable”). GPT-6 Astra got there for me too, and I think the new Gemini 4 Neon may count as well.

These now represent the baseline for what I expect from a frontier model.

#### 3D modeling and game development in September/October

Something interesting happened with frontier LLMs over just the past four months: they got _really good_ at 3D modeling. Set them up [with Blender](https://til.simonwillison.net/llms/blender-coding-agents-macos) or ask them to write Three.js code and they’ll produce credible models of almost anything you ask for.

I first noticed this with Claude Fable 5, but it really kicked into gear with Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and most recently the Gemini 4 family. Here’s [Gemini 4 Neon’s attempt](https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/gemini-4-neon-yonkers/index.html) at “Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data”, for example.

3D spatial awareness is crucial if you want to use vision LLMs for robotics. I don’t know if 3D modeling capabilities are a side-effect of the labs focusing on that or vice-versa.

Back in August I experimented with [having Fable 5 build me a raccoon heist game](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/5/raccoon-heist/). It had 3D graphics, looked like a game, and played really poorly. GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra [did a much better job](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/7/moonlight-mayhem/) but the game itself was still pretty dull after the first 90 seconds of play.

I was somewhat relieved that designing a game that was _fun_ appeared to remain a uniquely human pursuit. I even used that [in a talk](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/27/2026-in-llms-so-far/#simon-willison-2026-in-llms.059.webp) in September to reassure people that us humans still had a role to play!

Then, I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 “This game isn’t fun enough yet. Make it a LOT more fun.” [And it worked](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/20/battledrones/#v4-the-fun-update). My Command & Conquer-style RTS went from boring to deeply entertaining overnight, after Opus spent 12 hours playtesting new features and rebalancing the gameplay.

Opus 5.5 was the first model I’d used that appeared to understand fun. I’ve since worked on [several little game projects](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/28/vibe-game-development/) where prompts like “Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful” produced results that kept me engaged for significant amounts of time.

Opus 5.5 came out on September 22nd, 2026. I’ve been to two different conferences since then where people showed me game projects they’d been working on that really did feel like proper, worthwhile games.

The indie games scene has descended into a [full-blown culture war](https://kotaku.com/big-walk-ai-disclosure-igf-awards-vg-chat-2000755514) over AI-assisted programming. A lot of people are calling GTA VI [the last pre-generative AI blockbuster](https://gamingbolt.com/gta-6-is-the-last-pre-ai-blockbuster-video-game-of-its-kind-says-former-take-two-ceo).

It feels like another inflection point to me.

#### Is Fable 5.2 an inflection point too?

I’m still trying to decide if Fable 5.2 represents a new inflection point, or just another incremental improvement.

I’m getting _so much_ done with that model right now!

It seems to have taste that almost exactly matches my own. I have been burning through all sorts of gnarly problems that I’ve been thinking about (or procrastinating on) for several years now. The release notes for Datasette [1.0a42](https://docs.datasette.io/en/latest/changelog.html#a42-2026-11-08), [1.0a43](https://docs.datasette.io/en/latest/changelog.html#a43-2026-11-15), and [1.0a44](https://docs.datasette.io/en/latest/changelog.html#a44-2026-11-22)—plus LLM [0.37](https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#v0-37), [0.37.1](https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#v0-37-1), [0.37.2](https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#v0-37-2), [0.37.3](https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#v0-37-3), and [0.38](https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#v0-38)—_all in the last three weeks_, represent a flood of fixes, features and improvements.

If this does represent an inflection point, the key feature seems to be that _if you can imagine and then clearly describe a piece of software, Fable can build it_. That’s a wild thing to say, but it matches my experience over the past few weeks.

Software development has transformed beyond recognition in the last year. I don’t think I’ll ever go back to typing most of my code by hand.
